_about: Compliance rules as data, read by tools/policy.py (build.py and comply.py). brief.json compliance.jurisdictions names codes from 'jurisdictions' (or 'all'); a code also brings in its parent. A requirement applies when 'when' matches: 'in' (any selected code), 'flags' (all true) and 'not' (all false). Flags come from brief.json compliance{} (policy.py flags()). Cover patterns are English regular expressions, checked on the built page text when brief.lang is English. This is the kit's design-level reading of each law: it makes sure the pages, links and patterns exist and work. It is not legal advice; a lawyer approves the words (compliance.legal_review). Add a jurisdiction or a rule here, with the self-test passing (G10).

privacy-choices.title: Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information

requirements.why: Every listed privacy law requires a notice; the kit treats it as a baseline.
EU WAD and EAA, UK PSBAR, Israel reg. 35 and France RGAA require a statement; the kit treats it as a baseline.
Every production site needs a not-found page that keeps the header, footer and a way on.
Anything beyond what the site needs to work (analytics, advertising, embedded media) must be listed and explained.
CCPA/CPRA and state laws: an opt-out of sale, sharing and targeted advertising.
Impressum, Offenlegung, mentions légales, aviso legal.
E-Commerce Directive Art. 5, UK reg. 6, Swiss UWG: who runs the site, where, and how to reach them.
Selling online needs terms of sale.
Accounts need terms of use.
Recommended for every site.
Consumer Rights Directive and UK Consumer Contracts Regulations: the 14-day right to cancel.
Recommended wherever goods are sold.
Delivery costs and times before checkout.
PAIA: the access-to-information manual must be available on the website.

requirements.why: Nothing beyond what the site needs runs before a choice; reject is as easy as accept; no ticked boxes; choices can be changed later (GDPR, ePrivacy, PECR, LGPD, Law 25 and the rest of the opt-in group; the kit applies it everywhere).
A Global Privacy Control signal opts the visitor out of sale and sharing.
CCPA regulations: the footer link reads 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' or 'Your Privacy Choices'.
Italy: the VAT number (Partita IVA) on the site, in the footer by convention.
France RGAA: the compliance status ('Accessibilité : non / partiellement / totalement conforme') on every page.
Every required page is linked from the footer of every page.
Every outside host is declared in compliance.third_parties (the data inventory); nothing outside 'necessary' loads before a choice.
A form that collects personal data links the privacy notice; no box comes ticked.
A strict Content Security Policy works: no inline scripts or event handlers, no javascript: links, no insecure resources; security.txt (RFC 9116) is published.
site_url, canonical links, favicon, robots.txt and sitemap.xml.

manual.item: A lawyer reviews every policy page and the consent wording, then compliance.legal_review is set to done
Keyboard-only and screen-reader tests (VoiceOver, NVDA) on every page and on the consent banner
Real-browser checks in Safari, Firefox, Edge, iOS Safari and Android Chrome (only Chromium is automated)
Server headers from compliance/headers/ deployed, then confirmed on the live site (any header scanner)
security.txt Expires renewed before it lapses (the build sets it one year ahead)
A data processing agreement with each processor in the data inventory
Cookie names and lifetimes on the cookie page match what the live site sets
Records of processing (GDPR Art. 30) list the site's uses of personal data
A data protection impact assessment, if any use is high risk (GDPR Art. 35)
Form submissions reach an endpoint that is declared, secured and covered by the privacy notice
Email sign-up uses double opt-in, says what will be sent, and every email has an unsubscribe link (CAN-SPAM, CASL, GDPR)
Age check and verifiable parental consent before collecting a child's data (COPPA, GDPR Art. 8)
Payment pages: an inventory and integrity check of every script (PCI DSS 4.0, 6.4.3 and 11.6.1)
Consumer information on the accessibility of the service, as the European Accessibility Act requires
Quebec: French version of every page, and the person in charge of personal information named
Universal opt-out signals honoured on the server too (logs, CRM), not only in the browser
